apps.name: Nightshade
apps.summary: Switch emulation on PS5, built on ProsperoEden and Eden, with its own fixes and look.
apps.author: Oliv3rmoon

release.notes:
**Big games start right away, and the emulator gives memory back.** Tears of the Kingdom built the 16,000 pipelines it saved in earlier sessions for about 200 seconds at every start before it played, however often it had started before. Now a game starts as soon as its graphics are ready, and its saved pipelines are built while it plays. And a TOTK session that ended after 1.5 hours on v1.010.005 ("heap exhausted") should no longer end that way. Not measured on a console yet: start TOTK twice, play as long as you can, and send `/data/prosperoeden/logs`. The new `EDEN_SHADER_START` lines in `stderr.log` say where the start's time went, and the `heap:` lines what the emulator holds of the console's memory.

### Fixes

- **The game starts while its shader cache is built.** With the Vulkan renderer a game no longer waits for its saved pipelines: they are read and built behind it on the spare CPUs, and the game takes each one as soon as it is built. One it needs sooner it builds itself, as it does any new effect: with **Asynchronous shaders** on, that effect is missing for a moment; with them off, the game pauses for it. Leaving the game in the middle stops the build at once. `"background_shader_cache": false` in the settings file builds the whole cache before the game starts, as before (see [the settings](https://github.com/Oliv3rmoon/Nightshade/blob/v1.010.006/docs/SETTINGS.md#the-shader-cache-while-the-game-plays)). `stderr.log` says `Shader cache: the game starts now`, then how far the build is every 5 seconds, then `Shader cache ready: ... built while the game ran`.
- **Building the cache should be faster.** In every TOTK log the build ran at about 200 pipelines a second for its first 3,000, then at about 60, and letting the builders use every CPU in v1.010.004 hardly helped. The most likely reason: each of the 15 building threads has 8 MiB of memory of its own for its small allocations, what it built filled that after a few thousand pipelines, and from then on all of them allocated through the one lock every thread shares. A thread whose memory is full now takes another 8 MiB of its own. `EDEN_SHADER_START_HEAP` in `stderr.log` counts the allocations that still go through the shared lock.
- **The cache file is read in 8 MiB pieces, and only as fast as it is built.** It was read 4 KiB at a time, asking the file again for every entry: reading TOTK's took 15 seconds. And the whole file was queued at once, so the start held most of it in memory (the emulator's memory grew by 1.9 GB while TOTK's cache was built, and it keeps what it grows by); now at most a few pipelines per building thread wait to be built.

apps.summary: Media Player Classic Home Cinema ported to the PS5, using FFmpeg to play your own video files.
apps.author: MisterTemaki

release.notes:
## Media Player Classic PS5 1.5.2

Fixes from a full code review. Nothing changes in how you use the player.

### Fixed

- **C++ exceptions inside the app.**
  - Up to 1.5.1 the app's C++ runtime was half its own and half the console's. A C++ error thrown inside the app would have crashed it; Stella PS5 1.0 crashed that way starting any game.
  - The whole runtime is now the app's own, and the build refuses an eboot that takes any of it from the console.
  - A memory request that fails is now an error the code can handle, instead of stopping the app.
  - With Debug logs on, `boot.log` says `[boot] exceptions: ok` at the start, and a SIGSYS crash is in the crash log.
- **A thread the console refuses** (it caps how many an app has) ended the app. Now that file fails to open with a message, or plays with less (no sound, no disc read-ahead, tone mapping on fewer threads), and the app runs on.
- **Blu-ray `.sup` and VobSub (`.idx` + `.sub`) subtitle files** beside a film, or opened with File > Load Subtitle, never loaded. They load now. VobSub works from the console's own storage only, not from a share or a disc.
- **Bitmap subtitles (Blu-ray PGS, DVD, DVB) used too much memory.** Every picture of every bitmap track was kept for the whole film: gigabytes by the end of a Blu-ray remux with many PGS tracks.
  - Over 256 MB, pictures of lines more than 30 s away are dropped and decoded again when needed.
  - A subtitle line replayed after seeking back ends at the right time again.
- **Updates.**
  - `update.journal` now checks each replaced file's whole SHA-256, not its first MB. A journal left by 1.5.1 is still understood.
  - The "a newer version is available" notification no longer holds up the window.
- **Passwords on the screen.** Network passwords no longer show in:
  - File > Open File...'s list of recent files;
  - the title bar;
  - Recent Files;
  - failure messages and notifications.

  The addresses still open with their passwords.
- **Damaged or made-up files.**
  - A font with absurd glyph sizes isn't drawn at gigabyte sizes.
  - An audio file's cover over 8192 pixels a side isn't decoded; the logo shows instead.
  - File > Save Image of a file with `%2F` in its name keeps the picture in the screenshots folder.
- **Building.** Changed assets and a new version number are rebuilt without a `make clean`. The unused CRT shaders left over from the emulator ports are out of the app.

### Updating

- **From 1.5.1:** Help > Check for updates offers 1.5.2. Or send `MediaPlayerClassicPS5-v1.5.2.elf` to your payload loader (port 9021).
- Put the new ELF in your autoload when you can: it carries the new helper.

### Files

apps.name: Mediathek
apps.summary: Movie library that finds films in a movies folder on internal or USB storage, fetches posters from TMDB and plays them.
apps.author: M0S4YSH3LL0

release.notes:
## Mediathek 0.3.0 (`01.000.030`)

A Netflix-style movie library and player for the PS5. Put your films in a `movies` folder on the internal drive, a USB stick or extended storage; Mediathek finds them, shows a billboard and shelves with their posters, fetches covers and descriptions from TMDB, and plays them. English and German.

### What's new in 0.3.0

- **A richer details page.** It now shows the film's **length**, **video format** (codec, resolution, container), **sound format**, TMDB's **user score** (out of 10) and its **genres** (next to the collection above the title).
- **Languages.** An **Audio** row lists the audio languages of the tracks the app can actually decode, and a **Subtitles** row shows the language of the `.srt` file beside the film, read from its file name (`Film (2011).de.srt`, `Film.English.srt`). A track that does not play is not offered. Untagged tracks show "Unknown language".
- **Read from the file, once.** Length, formats and audio languages are read with FFmpeg when the page opens (headers only, no decoding) and cached, so reopening is instant. "Refresh cover and info" reads the file again.
- **Fewer TMDB requests.** Covers, wallpapers and descriptions are fetched only for films that have no cover; a rescan or restart no longer asks about films that already have one. Films that were fetched before get their score and genres once.

### Features

- **Home:** a billboard for the focused film, tinted by its colours, then shelves: Continue Watching, Recently Added, collections, decades and All Movies.
- **Movies:** an eight-column grid, sortable by title, newest or year.
- **Player:** scrubber, seeking, pause, audio-track and `.srt` subtitle switching, a stream info panel. It remembers where you stopped; 92% counts as watched.
- **Automatic covers:** with a free TMDB key, posters, wallpapers and descriptions are fetched for films that lack them. Pictures you put beside a film always win.
- **Names are read for you:** `Blue Harbor (2011).mkv` and `blue.harbor.2011.2160p.BluRay.x265-GRP.mkv` both work.

### Good to know

- Needs a PS5 that runs homebrew, with a loader that starts apps from `/data/homebrew` and an ELF loader on `127.0.0.1:9021`. Without it the app starts but finds no films.
- Checked on the author's console: start-up, the scan, cover and description download, the details page with its length, formats, score, genres and languages, and a large 1080p H.264 MKV playing with sound.
- **Not yet checked on a console:** the console language detection, 4K and HEVC playback (software decoding, not expected to be smooth), subtitle and audio-track switching, menu sound and rumble, and drives other than the author's.
- Only one `.srt` per film is used. Embedded subtitle tracks are not shown.

release.notes:
Two archives to listen to, and a scroller that tells you what is playing.

## Modland as a second source

Triangle now asks which archive first, then which station. The two are kept
apart because they are organised differently: the Mod Archive by genre and
chart, Modland by curated playlist.

Modland is read through its playlists, which are plain text files of direct
links. Eight stations: the favourites of around 850 modules, a chiptune
selection, netlabel releases, a couple of musicdisks and a demoparty compo.

## The scroller says what is playing

The greeting runs its one pass at startup and is never cut short. After that
the band carries the track: title, source, the tracker that wrote the module,
channels, instruments, patterns, running time, and the genre and artist where
the archive gave them. A new track fades the band out, swaps the line and
fades it back in.

## Visualiser

Stepping through presets follows a shuffled order instead of the alphabet.
Sorted by filename, stepping meant working through one author at a time. The
visualiser also moves on by itself every minute; L2 + Options turns that off.

## Keep a track

L2 + Circle writes the playing module into `music/` and adds it to
`index.txt`, so a tune that would otherwise scroll out of the 20 track history
can be kept.

## Fixed

The interface named The Mod Archive everywhere, including while downloading
from Modland. Each track now carries where it came from.

## Installing

Copy the contents of `PPSA01153.zip` to `/data/homebrew/PPSA01153/`, reload
the jailbreak chain and start it from the home screen. The 552 MilkDrop
presets are in the zip; `OliSePlayer-presets.zip` is the same pack on its own,
for adding to an install made without it.

Drop your own modules in `music/` and add their names to `music/index.txt`:
the sandbox will not let the app list a folder, so it reads that index.

release.notes:
## wiliwili PS5 v1.6.0.1

Native Homebrew title application for PlayStation 5 (Title ID: `PPSA99099`).
This release brings compatibility fixes for DLNA casting, resolves critical crashes during search input and application exit, and enhances the home screen presentation with native 4K backgrounds and a full-bleed icon.

---

### 🚀 Key Improvements & Fixes

#### 1. 📡 DLNA Casting Compatibility on PS5
- **Sandbox Network & Port Adaptation**: Adapted to PS5 sandbox network policies with reworked port probing and binding logic, resolving socket option errors and ensuring reliable casting service startup.

release.notes:
## PSP5 01.000.100

PSP5 now follows the console's language, reads games and texture packs from USB drives, and lets you remap the PSP's buttons.

### Interface language

Choose a language under **Settings → System → Language** and the home screen follows it, not just the emulator. 45 languages are available, including Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Lao. The font atlases were rebuilt to carry them, growing from 113 glyphs to 3,055 per face. Right-to-left languages are laid out right-to-left.

Where PPSSPP already translates a term, PSP5 uses its translation. The remainder — favourites, the A–Z view, the cheat panel, the save-state slots, the button names and the description under every settings row — are PSP5's own, shipped as 78 strings in 44 languages under `assets/lang/psp5/`.

**These 78 strings are machine-translated and unreviewed in most languages.** Corrections are a one-line edit in `assets/lang/psp5/<id>.ini`: the files are plain `English = translation`, and a missing line falls back to English.

### Games and texture packs on USB drives

PSP5 now reads drives using the same layout as its own memory stick:

```
/mnt/usb0/PSP/GAME/<your game>.iso        # also .cso, .chd, EBOOT.PBP
/mnt/usb0/PSP/TEXTURES/<DISC_ID>/         # a texture pack, with its textures.ini
```

All eight USB ports (`/mnt/usb0` … `/mnt/usb7`) and both extended drives (`/mnt/ext0`, `/mnt/ext1`) are scanned. A texture pack on a drive takes precedence over one on the memory stick.

**This requires folder listing to be unlocked.** A PS5 app can open a file by its full path but cannot list a folder, and finding games requires listing. PSP5 requests the unlock at every start, and any of these will grant it: **etaHEN** (enable *Legacy CMD server* in its toolbox), **OnionHEN**, **LegacyJB**, or the **PS5SX2 Helper** (add PSP5 to its `/data/whitelist.txt`).

Without it, PSP5 runs from its own memory stick as before and USB drives appear empty. The reason is recorded in `psp5.log` as `unlock: nothing answered`.

### Button remapping

**Settings → Controls → Buttons** lists all twelve PSP buttons — the four face buttons, both shoulders, Start, Select and the four D-pad directions — with the console button each is mapped to.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Cross** | set the button |
| **Square** | set a second button |
| **Triangle** | clear the second |
| **Circle** | back |

Each PSP button can be mapped to **two** console buttons, so Select can sit on both the touch pad and L3, or L on both L1 and L2.

  request sent without data made the network library wait for keyboard input that never comes on
  a console. MW2 now reaches its menu and searches Xbox LIVE matches through the Xenia server.

  answer can no longer freeze a game, and each request is written to the game's log with its
  result and time.
- Games' own non-blocking sockets now really do not wait on the PS5.
- **Router ports:** the PS5 does not let programs use ports below 1024, so a game's port 1000 is
  opened as 11000 on the console. The automatic router request (UPnP) now asks for the game's
  port towards the real one (1000 to 11000). Many routers refuse ports below 1024 that way
  (`UPnP error code 501` in the log); then add the forwarding rules by hand on the router, UDP, to
  your PS5's address: 1000 to 11000, 1001 to 11001, 1013 to 11013 (MW2's; the log's
  `XSocket::Bind` lines show each game's).

Checked on a PS5: Halo 3 online (sessions, connection checks, leaderboards) and MW2 searching
and finding other players' Xbox LIVE matches. Not confirmed yet: joining and playing a whole match
with other people. Please send the game's log from `PPSA50011/logs` with your results.

## Changed

- **A new install looks and runs as the PlayStation did**: the software renderer at the console's resolution, its interlacing, the cracks between polygons, the edges a television hid cropped, no texture pack, the CPU's instruction cache. An install from before keeps its settings.
- **Picture presets**: Original, Original on a TV (composite signal, curved picture tube), Fast (2x), Normal (4x), Enhanced (6x), Beautiful (8x) and Speedrun.
- **The CPU's instruction cache as the PlayStation has it**: a line takes 4 to 7 cycles to fill from RAM (it took 1 cycle a word), and the same code reached through either of its addresses is cached once.

PC5 2.0.2 brings the mouse wheel, a button that slows the pointer, and fixes from your reports.

### Install

- **ProsperoStore**: update PC5 from its page in the store.
- **PC5's own updater**: **Settings › System › Update now**, or **Update now** when PC5 asks as it opens. It downloads only what changed when you have the version before, otherwise the whole app. PC5 restarts by itself when the update is installed.

### What's new

- **Mouse wheel**: a USB mouse's wheel now reaches the game. With a game on **Keyboard & mouse**, any button can also be **Wheel up** or **Wheel down** in **△ › Button mapping** (after the mouse buttons in the key list): each press turns the wheel one notch, for a visual novel's rollback or a map's zoom.
- **Slow pointer button**: in **△ › Button mapping**, with a stick moving the pointer, **Slow pointer button** picks a button that slows the pointer while you hold it, for placing and aiming precisely. **Slower by** sets how much, 10 % to 90 % (50 % by default).

### Fixes from your reports

- **No sound device found**: the console's speakers now have a hardware ID, as Windows reports one. A game's system check that asks for it no longer says there is no sound device.
- **Direct3D 12 detection**: Unreal Engine 5 games that keep Direct3D 12's Agility SDK in `D3D12\x64` beside their program now draw with Direct3D 12 too.
- Everything else in 2.0.1 is unchanged.

### Which games run

See the [game compatibility list](https://github.com/bornaradusin/PC5/wiki/Game-compatibility), made from players' reports and issues. Got a game running? [Add it](https://github.com/bornaradusin/PC5/discussions/new?category=game-compatibility): the form takes a minute.

### Reporting a problem

Please report problems as an [issue on GitHub](https://github.com/bornaradusin/PC5/issues/new/choose), not in ProsperoStore's comments:
- **A game doesn't run** for a game.
- **A problem with PC5** for PC5 itself.

Attach the game's zip from `/data/prospero-win/logs/`: an `issue-…zip`, or the game's newest `log-…zip` when nothing crashed. The form asks for it, as the cause can't be found without it. **△** on PC5's crash message opens the form for you, filled in.

If an update from PC5 fails, the message says why. Turn on **Settings › System › Keep all logs**, try again and attach PC5's own log. See [Logs and debugging](https://github.com/bornaradusin/PC5/wiki/Logs-and-debugging) for what an issue may ask for.

### Not supported

- Games that need a store's launcher or client running (Steam, EA app, Ubisoft Connect, Rockstar Games Launcher).
- Anti-cheat, games that need kernel drivers, and DRM-protected games.
- .NET programs that mix .NET and C++ (C++/CLI).
- 16-bit Windows and DOS programs.

## New

- **Frame generation** with [MihawkGen](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_MihawkGen), thanks to [mihawk-99](https://github.com/mihawk-99): `[display] framegen = 2` (or `3`, `4`) shows 2x (3x, 4x) the frames a Vulkan game presents. DXVK, Zink and Vulkan games all work ([#722](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/722)).
- **Direct3D 12** through vkd3d-proton 3.0.1: `wine: {dxvk: true, vkd3d: true}` in an install script. Feature level 11_1 on the console ([#711](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/711)).
- **In-game menu** on L3+R3 (`[display] menu`), with a **keyboard input** entry. A **two-finger touchpad click** opens the PS5's on-screen keyboard and types the line into the game ([#707](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/707), [#726](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/726)).
- **Single-program titles:** one Windows program as its own app on the home screen, without the launcher ([#719](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/719)).
- **A second DualSense** as a second keyboard player ([#427](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/427)).

## Controls

- Hold **Options + Create** for 3 seconds to close a game ([#720](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/720)).
- The touchpad's left half is **Back** and its right half is **Guide**; mouse **wheel** works ([#721](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/721), [#715](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/715)).

## Memory and fixes

- Games see the console's real memory (12 GiB), instead of almost none, which some games refused to start with ([#688](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/688)).
- Wine's own heap moved out of the game's flexible memory, leaving 5–26 MB more of it for the game ([#470](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/470), thanks to [leolobato](https://github.com/leolobato)).
- Thread and fiber stacks use what Windows uses: 3000 fibers take 49 MB instead of 3.1 GB. 64-bit games can reserve up to 512 GiB of address space ([#727](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/727), with leolobato's patch).

## Snes9x PS5 2.10

### New

- **Search by name on the shelf.** **Circle** opens the on-screen keyboard. Type part of a game's name, choose Done, and the shelf shows only the games that match.
  - Capitals and accents don't matter: `pokemon` finds *Pokémon*.
  - The file name counts too.
  - The shelf shows what you searched and how many games match (`Search: mario (3)`). Circle again changes or clears it.
  - With no match, the shelf says so and how to get every game back.
  - The search stays while you change tabs or play, and is gone when the app quits.
- **The shelf opens at once.** "Looking for games..." no longer comes up every time the shelf opens.
  - The app saves the game list (`/data/snes9x/library.bin`) and opens from it next time. It checks the folders in the background, with nothing on screen, and the shelf updates quietly if a game was added or removed.
  - Back from a game there is no scan at all. It only checks again if a USB drive or a share was plugged in or removed while you played.
  - The first start after installing still scans as before, once.
  - A game picked after its file was deleted says "The file is no longer there." and goes back to the shelf.

### Fixed (from a full code audit)

- **C++ exceptions.**
  - The app's C++ runtime was split between its own copy and the console's. This is the mix that made Stella PS5 1.0 crash at its first exception. It is now entirely the app's own, and every build checks it.
  - When memory runs out while a ROM is loaded or a state is saved or loaded, that load or save fails with a message.
  - A damaged state file can no longer make the app ask for gigabytes of memory.
- **Updates with ShadowMountPlus.**
  - When ShadowMountPlus runs the app from another folder (a USB or extended drive), an update, from Settings > Updates or a new payload, now goes into that folder. Up to 2.9 it went into `/data/homebrew/PPSA99922`, so the copy the console runs stayed old.
  - Without ShadowMountPlus, updates go to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99922` as before.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - the shelf could hang if the system refused a thread;
  - the update download is checked more strictly (sizes, no HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect);
  - the crash log now also catches SIGSYS;
  - update error messages are translated and no longer cut off;
  - the build rebuilds what a version change needs.

### Updating

- **From 2.9:** Settings > Updates offers 2.10. Or send `Snes9xPS5-v2.10.elf` to your payload loader (port 9021).
- Put the new ELF in your autoload when you can: it carries the new helper.

## Prospero Explorer v1.0

### What is Prospero Explorer

Prospero Explorer is a file explorer for the PS5 console, built on the SharpProspero SDK. It browses and manages the file system, unpacks and builds archives, plays audio and video, views and edits text, views and converts pictures, installs packages from the writable area and from removable devices, launches an installed title, serves the whole file system over the network, opens a web address, and reports what the machine is doing.

### How to install & launch

- Unzip the file ```ProsperoExplorer-v1.zip``` **into a folder** and **move/copy the folder** to ```/homebrew``` on your USB **OR** ```/data/homebrew``` on the console
- Install using [dump_installer](https://github.com/EchoStretch/dump_installer)
- Launch from home screen

### Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Browsing | Listing with sizes and kinds, sorting, hidden names, find within a folder, multiple selection, copy, cut, paste, rename, delete, new folder, new file, properties, checksums |
| Archives | Browse and unpack zip and tar, unpack a lone gzip or zlib stream, build a zip or tar from a selection |
| Media | Audio and video playback with seeking, looping, volume and tags; WAV and VAG play through the decoders when the player will not take them |
| Text | Viewer with line numbers, wrapping, a hex view and a table view for comma- or tab-separated files; editing by line, find, go to line, save and save as |
| Pictures | PNG, JPEG, BMP, TGA and GIF; fit modes, panning and pinch-zoom by touch, rotate, flip, grayscale, invert, brightness, contrast, blur, a screenshot of the view, and conversion between every form that can be written |
| Packages | Finds installable files in the writable area and on removable devices, installs them, reports whether a title is already present, and launches an installed title by its id |
| Network | A file service over the network reaching the whole file system, with optional login, a read-only mode and a root it cannot climb above |

apps.name: PS5SD
apps.summary: Runs stable-diffusion.cpp on the console's GPU, with a web UI and a TV dashboard.
apps.author: Darkatek7

release.notes:
PS5SD 1.0.0 is the version that keeps its promises: every item of the 1.0 checklist in [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/Darkatek7/PS5SD/blob/v1.0.0/ROADMAP.md#100-ready-done) holds. From here on, a change that breaks a client of the API needs a new major version.

## What 1.0 means

- **The API is fixed**: one error shape with a code, progress as server-sent events, `POST /sdapi/v1/options` waits for the model, the `model` of an OpenAI request switches it, and an OpenAPI description at `/ps5sd/v1/app/openapi.json` (0.9.15 to 0.9.17).
- **No run fails without a reason**: the web UI says before a run when it may not fit and what to lower; a run that fails anyway says why (0.9.18).
- **No known crash**: the two ends 0.9.18's measurements found are fixed, and there is no open bug.

## An update keeps everything

- Tested on the console from every release since 0.5.0 (26 releases): install the old one, make models, LoRAs, presets, images, settings and an API key through its API, update to 1.0, and check that all of it is still there. All 26 passed. `scripts/update-test.py` does it again for any build.

## A soak test

- 38 minutes of mixed load on the console: 22 model switches between Z-Image Turbo, SDXL, FLUX.2 Klein 9B with a LoRA and Wan 2.1, 36 jobs with three queued at once, a cancel while a job runs, a video, and an event stream open all along. Every job and switch did what it should, each round took the same time, and the CPU heap stayed at 0.63 to 0.66 GiB after the first round. `scripts/soak-test.py` runs it again. The numbers are in [CONSOLE.md](https://github.com/Darkatek7/PS5SD/blob/v1.0.0/docs/CONSOLE.md#a-soak-test-before-10-2026-10-28).

## A home screen background of its own

- The placeholder background is gone: ribbons of blue, violet and pink light, made by PS5SD itself on the console with FLUX.2 Klein 4B. A home screen theme that shows its own picture for every app still wins.

## The docs

- New screenshots of the web UI in the README, on a PC and a phone.

## Install

Install from the homebrew store, or unpack `PPSA99576.zip` into `/data/homebrew/` on the console and let ShadowMountPlus scan. An update from any 0.x release keeps your models, presets, gallery and settings.

Next: see [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/Darkatek7/PS5SD/blob/v1.0.0/ROADMAP.md#after-10).

apps.name: TokenStation5
apps.summary: Makes the console an AI endpoint over Tailscale, on its own Vulkan inference engine.
apps.author: ThatRetiredDude

release.notes:
## Security fixes in 01.004.001

This update fixes security holes in TokenStation5's built-in Tailscale. Update if you use Tailscale to reach your PS5 (#97).

- **Your tailnet's access rules now apply.** Before, every device on your tailnet could reach the API, whatever the rules in your Tailscale admin console said. Now only devices your rules allow can connect, and none can until the rules arrive from Tailscale.
- **A way around the API key is closed.** A device on the tailnet that opened a connection and dropped it at the right moment could be let in without a key. Over Tailscale, every request now needs a key, as intended.
- **HTTPS no longer trusts the leaked eMudhra certificates** (Tailscale's bulletin TS-2026-013), for every connection the title makes: Tailscale, downloads and search.
- **Your Tailscale sign-in key is deleted from the settings file** once the PS5 has signed in, so it can't be read later over the home network's FTP.

About "Tailworm": those flaws are in Tailscale SSH and Serve in Tailscale's own `tailscaled`. TokenStation5 runs its own small Tailscale client, without SSH or Serve, so they don't apply to it.

Tested on a PS5 over Tailscale: a valid key works for chat, and no key, a wrong key or a deleted key is refused.

## Also in this version: everything new since 01.003.000

### Google's Gemma 3 12B
- **Gemma 3 runs on the PS5** (#94). Gemma 3 12B (bartowski's `google_gemma-3-12b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf`, 6.8 GB) passed every GPU check against the CPU and 59 of 60 app-style checks, tool calls and a write-a-file agent task included. Find it in the Models page's Hugging Face search.
- Most of its layers only look back 1,024 tokens, so they keep a small rolling memory, and it fits about **29,700 tokens of context** next to its weights.
- It reads prompts at **250 tokens a second** and writes about **40 a second**, up from 188 and 35 in its first build on the console.

### Faster and steadier
- New GPU kernels for wide attention heads and sliding windows: prompts read a third faster on Gemma, and writing is 13% faster (#94).
- Switching models no longer fails with "out of GPU memory" after a bigger model was loaded: the model's memory is now split into smaller pieces (#94).
- A GPU check on the model you're serving no longer runs out of memory (#94).

### Better answers out of the box
- **Known-good settings** (#92): each checked model (Qwen 3 8B, Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B, Llama 3.1 8B, Llama 3.2 3B, Mistral Nemo 12B and now Gemma 3 12B) gets the sampling settings that scored best on the PS5. An app's own settings still win.
- Four fixes to how tool calls and thinking are read back from the models (#92).
- **Mistral Nemo 12B takes tools** in its own format (#91).
